index_table.label: Index table (moves with mech; drawn only without it)

machine.label: Machine of primitives (moves by joints, couplings and drivers of mech; schema 2 only, needs mech)

part_sink.label: Workpiece sink (removes a part in its zone)

part_source.label: Workpiece source (a part appears on the make bit or a click)

robot_arm.label: Robot arm (signals by the shared schema) (moves with mech; drawn only without it)

servo_axis.label: Servo axis (signals by the shared schema) (moves with mech; drawn only without it)

zone_sensor.label: Presence sensor (ON while a workpiece is in its zone)

catalog.layout_note: Millimetres, y is up, y = 0 is the floor. A device pose.pos is the bottom centre of the device. Each part has size [x,y,z] and pos = offset of the part's bottom centre from the device pose.pos (override with the device `parts` field: {part: {pos, rot}}). A port `at` is the offset from the bottom centre of its part. A cylinder lies along x. Rotation is about y (pose.rot[1]). Parts are static: a stroke is not part of the size. Put devices on the floor (pos y 0) or on top of another device, keep boxes from overlapping, and draw air links valve_a -> cap and valve_b -> rod (a device with a valve and no links gets these by default).
catalog.params_note: A param is {type:number, min, max, default}, {type:enum, values, default} or {type:bool, default}. timing:true kinds also take timing {lag_ms, fwd_ms, back_ms (0 to 60000), source}.

index_table.label: Index table: each pulse on run turns one station (360 / stations) in move_ms after lag_ms

robot_6r.label: 6-axis arm (generic figure of 10-architecture 12.5, no link offsets): plays a taught pose by a program number

servo_screw.label: Ball-screw axis: the carriage follows a commanded position; the motor turns once for each lead_mm of travel

wheeled_base.label: Two-wheel base: the wheels turn by a program; the base follows by differential drive (no slip)

catalog.presets_note: A preset is a template of the device key `mech`: pick it with mech {preset, args, sensors?, basis?}. `args` are the preset's own values (arg_order is their order); a number field may be {arg, mul}. The server expands it to joints, couplings, drivers and sensors (facts.mech[].expanded). A preset gives the same motion as the same explicit mech.

generic.source: Assumed ratios of the design study (docs/research/photo-twin/10-architecture.md 2.5): body_len 3.0 * bore + stroke (never below stroke + 20), body_dia 1.4 * bore, rod_dia 0.4 * bore, rod_out 2.0 * bore, pivot_back 1.5 * bore. No maker table; values marked ratio.

smc_cm2.source: SMC CM2 series, CAT.EUS20-269A-UK, page 8 Basic (Double-side Bossed) (B): S, I, D, H; page 12 Single Clevis (C): L (design 10-architecture.md 2.5). cylinder_single adds 25 mm to S for each started 50 mm of stroke (CAT.EUS20-269B-UK page 37). CDM2 (built-in magnet) is taken to have the same sizes: not verified.

signal_schema.active: high | low (bit signals only, default high)
signal_schema.device: bit: X, Y or M address; word and bcd: D address
signal_schema.dir: in | out (seen from the PLC: out = the PLC drives it, in = the PLC reads it)
signal_schema.name: 1 to 24 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -

frames.custom: a `solid` may add `frames` {name:{pos, rot, type}}; they are fixed in `base`
frames.moving: `out` (cyl, jaw) and `carriage` (linear) move with the axis value; every other frame is fixed in `base`

geometry_note: Units mm, degrees, ms. Right-handed axes. World +y is up, the floor is y = 0. A frame is an origin and three axes; every device has the frame `base` (for a catalog kind the bottom centre of the main part, +y away from the surface it stands on). rot [rx, ry, rz] means R = Ry(ry) * Rz(rz) * Rx(rx): ry is the heading about the parent +y (a positive angle turns +x toward -z), rz tilts the own +x above the parent x-z plane, rx rolls about the own +x. Test vectors: [0,-90,0] maps +x to [0,0,1]; [0,0,-90] maps +x to [0,-1,0]; [90,0,0] maps +y to [0,0,1] and +z to [0,-1,0]. world(datum of the child) = world(frame `on`) * T(pose.pos) * R(pose.rot); the datum is a frame of the device itself (key `datum`, default from the mount style), so pose places that frame, not `base`. A `surface` frame has +y out of the surface; an `axial` frame has +x out along an axis. A face frame of a box: look at the face from outside with the body upright; +x points right, +z points down, +y points at you. A cylinder or gripper lies along its +x: frames mid, cap_end, head_end, pivot and `out` (the rod end; it moves with the stroke). A belt carries along +x: frames surface, in, end. A linear servo axis moves its carriage along +x: the frame `carriage` moves with the axis value. `seat` is the bottom centre of a box kind with +x = body +y. Sizes come from named params (x_mm, y_mm, z_mm, bore_mm, stroke_mm, body_len_mm, length_mm ...); a size that the scene does not give is derived and `facts.dims` says how (given, series, ratio, default). Schema 2 only: `on` ("<id>" or "<id>.<frame>"), `mount`, `datum`, `basis`, `model`, kind `solid` with `shape` (box or cyl items) and `frames`, and the scene key `refs` (known lengths between two frames).

skin_recipe.note: A lamp that the PLC drives is a device of kind lamp. Its look is two groups of one address: the dark lamp while the bit is OFF, the lit lamp (tone mark) while it is ON.

guide.skin_rules: A skin is the look only: {groups:[{name (1-16 of a-z 0-9 _), frame (a frame of the same device, default base), show|hide (a bit pin "<device id>.<slot or signal>" of the model), items:[{t:box,size,pos,rot,tone}|{t:cyl,d,len,d2,axis,pos,rot,tone}]}]}. Items are in the coordinates of the frame of their group; a group on `out` moves with the rod, a group on `carriage` with the carriage. tone is one of `tones`; `mark` only in a group with `show`. At most 16 groups, 64 items and 16384 bytes for each device, 1000 skin items for the scene. A skin sets no size, place, travel, direction, address or timing: those are the skeleton. `indicators` shows the bits of other devices on a board: [{pins ["<device id>.<signal>", ...] (1-64 bit pins), at [x,y,z], step [dx,dy,dz], frame, d}], at most 8 rows and 128 lamps for each device.
guide.workpieces: Workpieces (schema 2, simulation only; rules, no physics). 1. Read the photo and the tones of `tones`. 2. Draft scene key `workpieces.types` {name: {shape round|square, d_mm or side_mm, h_mm, material metal|plastic, tone (a name of tones except mark), basis}}: one type for each shape, colour and size; sizes from a known length are basis ref, by eye guess; write material as you think and always basis guess, because a photo does not show metal. 3. Draft scene key `points` [{name (1-24 of a-z 0-9 _), on ("<id>" or "<id>.<frame>": the device that makes or holds the part there, so the point moves with it), pos [x,y,z] in that frame (the bottom centre of a part that rests there), catch_mm, holds, basis}]. 4. Device keys: `stack` {point, fed_by (a cylinder with a push rule from that point), content (type names, lowest first, at most 20), refill}; `push` [{from, to}] on a cylinder (at most 4); `stop` {at} on a conveyor or {belt, at} on a cylinder (active from half stroke); `sense` on a sensor, exactly one of {point, within_mm, material any|metal}, {held_by: a pad or gripper}, {pulse_of: a conveyor, mm_per_pulse}; scene key `workpieces.start` [{type, at}]. 5. Read facts.points, facts.workpieces, facts.push (contact_mm and end_gap_mm of each push rule) and ask: put the ask lines to the person (which colour is metal, one puck measured with a ruler), then draft again with basis user or measured. The person confirms the draft on the page. Limits: 32 points, 8 types, 20 start parts, 4 stacks, 16 push rules, 8 stops, 32 sensor rules, 50 parts at the start.

model_rules.rule: a photo is a file of the person; a model file names none
a module model is a PLC feature
its values are PLC addresses; every slot of the kind is a pin <id>.<slot>
a PLC address; the pin is <id>.<name>
a word address; use mech with the preset servo_screw and a word signal
one pin "<device id>.<signal>", not an address
pins: ["<device id>.<signal>", ...], not from and count
not a slot name of its kind: a pin name is used once

note: Read-only. A simulation pass is not a test on real equipment.

scene_schema.devices: array of at most 200: {id (1-32 of A-Z a-z 0-9 - _, unique), kind (a key of catalog.kinds), label, pose:{pos:[x,y,z] mm, rot:[x,y,z] deg}, params (per kind), timing:{lag_ms, fwd_ms, back_ms}, signals:[{name, dir, type, active}] (no device: a pin is <id>.<slot or signal name>), mech, skin (groups; show and hide take a pin), indicators (rows with pins), on, mount, datum, frames, shape, basis, model, stack, push, stop, sense}. A twin model holds no PLC address: no io, no signals[].device, no position, no scene photos or modules.
scene_schema.name: optional text, at most 40 characters
scene_schema.parts_and_links: device `parts`:{part_name:{pos:[x,y,z], rot:[x,y,z]}} (part names from catalog.layout[kind].parts); scene `links` (at most 400):[{from:"<device>.<port>", to:"<device>.<port>", kind:"air"|"wire"}] (ports from catalog.layout[kind].ports; both ends must have the link kind). See catalog.layout_note.
scene_schema.photos: optional array of at most 32: {file, camera:{pos:[x,y,z], target:[x,y,z], fov} | null}
scene_schema.schema: 1 or 2. Schema 2 adds, per device: on ("<id>" or "<id>.<frame>"; default the world), mount (a style of `mounts` that allows the form of the kind; default unknown; floor needs no `on`), datum (the frame of this device that pose places; default from the mount style, see `mounts[].datum`; never a moving frame), size params per kind (cylinders: series, body_len_mm, body_dia_mm, rod_dia_mm, rod_out_mm, pivot_back_mm, axis_h_mm: absent = derived, see `series`; servo_axis: stroke_mm, home_at, addr_grows, home_mm, lead_mm, carriage_len_mm, carriage_h_mm, body_h_mm, body_w_mm, body_len_mm; conveyor: length_mm, width_mm, height_mm, motor_at; box kinds: x_mm, y_mm, z_mm), basis ({param|pose|shape: user|label|measured|ref|guess}, at most 32), model (text, at most 40), and for kind `solid` shape (1 to 24 items {t:box,size,pos,rot} or {t:cyl,d,len,d2,axis,pos,rot}) and frames ({name:{pos, rot:[rx,ry,rz], type:surface|axial}}, at most 16). pose.rot has three angles in schema 2. Device keys `skin` (the look: groups of box/cyl items bound to a frame of the device, with show/hide by a pin of the scene and a tone from `tones`), `skin_source` (the server sets it: a model's skin is always `model`; only the person's page sets `checked`) and `indicators` (rows of lamps that repeat bits of other devices); the rules are in `guide.skin_rules`, the work order in `guide.order`. Scene key `refs` (at most 16 {a:"<id>.<frame>", b:"<id>.<frame>", mm, basis: measured|label}): a length that a person measured; the reply gives `scene_mm` for each. The reply of a schema 2 draft has `facts` (where each device stands in the world, its axis, `box_mm`, `dims` with their source, the axis tips), `ask` (what to put to the person), `notes`, `not_simulated` and `limits`; read them, do not trust your own arithmetic. See `geometry_note` and `frames`.
scene_schema.simulated_false: kinds with simulated:false are drawn and mapped, but the plant does not move them yet
